newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil seen down $1.25-$1.50, Brent steady.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil seen down $1.25-$1.50, Brent steady.

text.p: IPE May gas oil futures on Friday were expected to open $1.25-$1.50 a tonne lower, reflecting losses on the Brent contract just ahead of Thursday's close, brokers said.

June IPE Brent crude futures were called to open unchanged after shedding 23 cents in some late profit-selling on Thursday to close at $18.29 a barrel. SIMEX Brent on Friday had traded down two cents at $18.27.
"We saw some late selling, some profit-taking," said a broker.
May gas oil, having closed at $171 a tonne, would test technical support at $169.50, dealers said.
"I'd expect the trend to continue but no doubt we'll see a quiet morning as far as volume's concerned," said one.
Dealers said gas oil losses in Asia, where the market has led the world in recent weeks, looked set to undermine the IPE gas oil contract further.
The Indian Oil Corp (IOC) made an unexpectedly low award for June delivery of diesel to Asia. IOC bought 315,000 tonnes in seven cargoes, well below expectations of a 600,000 tonne purchase.
But the eastern gas oil market still was finding support from regional trade buyer Hin Leong.
Hin Leong, together with two other traders, had since March 3 bought almost 18 million barrels of physical gas oil.
But purchases so far this week have been slight compared to last week's one-day record of 2.44 million barrels purchased.
Speculations was that the companies were winding down their purchases.
Dealers said U.S. gasoline would help prop up the market after bucking the trend of other NYMEX and IPE futures contracts on Thursday to finish firmer.
